problem_type: Provider upload locator mismatches sealed reference snapshot
symptom: Browser approval of first/last keyframe video fails Reference URL snapshot does not match authorized assets before GPU submission
direct_cause: Web injects no-op localization returning nomi-local URLs; canonical Comfy upload returns an input filename rather than the HTTP URL required by authorization; Comfy upload used original filename with overwrite:true, allowing another reference to mutate a sealed URL; first content-addressing implementation introduced Node-only imports into a shared renderer module, reproduced by actual browser build and unit composer suites
class_root: Every production host must localize pinned assets through owning transport and convert successful provider upload receipts to canonical HTTP snapshot URLs before sealing
affected_population: Web and desktop reference-backed ProductionRun approvals
Same-asset first/last frames and multiple uploaded keyframes
entry_points: Desktop and MCP production authorization preparation

external_sources.purpose: Inspected upload/image receipt name/subfolder/type and view HTTP query protocol

invariants: Authorization accepts only HTTP snapshots for exact pinned reference identities
Provider locators must match actual successful upload receipts
Web and desktop use the same transport owner before sealing
Shared Comfy uploads use content-addressed filenames and never overwrite an existing input
Shared asset localization remains browser-importable and uses standard Web Crypto plus the existing pure MIME extension owner

door_reduction.why_not: Three production host entry points remain adapters to canonical reference owner; generic vendor localization callers and output URL builder remain distinct consumers of existing shared transports.

generality_proof: Canonical resolver owns receipt-to-HTTP transformation for every production caller and every admitted upload strategy; only the declared Comfy upload transport can return file locators, and every mapped locator requires its actual input receipt

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Pin assets, upload through owning transport, and provide sealed HTTP reference URLs
Canonical Comfy receipt HTTP URL encoding
Every Comfy upload caller uses content-addressed input names and overwrite:false

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Remove no-op resolver injection and use canonical production authorization default resolver
Desktop uses same canonical reference URL owner
Ordinary dispatch consumes provider-native uploaded filenames directly and does not seal HTTP authorization snapshots

recurrence.reason: Every locally materialized reference and every Comfy filename upload can reproduce snapshot mismatch
same_class_scan: Actual build:web red createHash not exported by __vite-browser-external plus seven browser composer failures preserved in QA build-web-final.log/full-test-final.log

prevention.invariant: Only HTTP URLs from matching real upload receipts or original HTTP transport outputs cross into production seal
prevention.failure_mode: Malformed or unmatched provider file locators reject before paid submission
prevention.strategy: Reuse asset ingestion, upload IO and canonical Comfy view formatter; delete web no-op bypass

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove the callable web no-op localization bypass

dependency_lifecycle.current: Installed ComfyUI upload/image and view protocol
dependency_lifecycle.target: Same supported upload receipt HTTP protocol
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Owning provider transport already reports all required facts; fix application snapshot contract rather than upgrade GPU runtime
exit_criteria: Changed upload receipt or view protocol must fail class tests and require owner adaptation before execution

migration: No stored plan migration. Existing failed approval can present a fresh quote and reapprove with exact pinned assets; sealed stale/non-HTTP authorization remains rejected.
residual_risks: Actual browser GPU first/last submission pending coordinator verification
Renderer build/browser suites must pass after shared Web Crypto correction
